title: Canonical proof-object fingerprint
problem: A dependency list can omit a changed proof-object component, allowing nominal certificate freshness despite semantic drift.
rules: Set-like collections are canonicalized before hashing so irrelevant ordering does not change identity.
Any semantic/support/trust/dependency change changes the SHA-256 proof-object fingerprint.
The fingerprint is an integrity/change detector, not a digital signature and not a truth/confidence score.
invariants: Proof Object Identity Must Cover Its Semantic Inputs
Unchanged IDs With Changed Meaning != Same Proof Object
boundary: A hash can show that two declared proof objects differ; it cannot establish that either object is correct or that an attacker has not supplied a consistently false object.
